title: Redwood PLG Quickstart Discovery - Solstice AI
summary: Intro discovery for Solstice AI evaluating Redwood's PLG quickstart & self-serve API. AE+SE overview: account setup, free credits, SDKs, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, security requirements (SOC2, KMS, VPC). Customer priority: fast POC for chat feature, predictable latency for low-latency user-facing inference, and data residency for EU users.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private fit

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Harper Nguyen (Redwood CSM); Raj Patel (CTO, Solstice AI), Marta Gomez (ML Eng), Oliver Reed (Head of Infra)

Summary: quick discovery focused on self-serve PLG quickstart, free credits, and time-to-first-token for a chat POC. Customer has EU users and some data residency needs, also wants predictable latency and cost guidance.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, quick intros, then we'll go through a short quickstart overview and see what fit looks like for solstice.
[00:10] Raj Patel: yep thanks, i'm raj, cto. we want to spin up a chat POC fast, get time to first token low, and see how the hosted api works before we consider dedicated capacity.
[00:20] Maya Chen: perfect — we typically get teams running in under an hour with our quickstart, free credits on sign up, node and python sdk snippets, and a sample app. liam will walk through the tech bits after high level.
[00:35] Liam O'Connor: hi all, liam here, i'm the solutions engineer. quick note: time-to-first-token depends on model choice and whether you use streaming; for small chat POC you can expect ~100-200ms token latencies for redwood hosted on common models, but it varies.
[00:55] Marta Gomez: sorry quick q, are those numbers for hosted or dedicated?
[01:00] Liam O'Connor: those are hosted averages on our curated open models. dedicated can give more consistent p99s if you need strict slos, and private (vpc/on-prem) is possible for data residency or compliance.
[01:20] Oliver Reed: on residency, our users are EU-only, and we need to ensure logs/audit and data at rest are handled in eu regions. do you offer region pinning for hosted?
[01:32] Maya Chen: yes, we have eu regions for hosted and you can pin requests to regionally isolated endpoints; for stricter controls we recommend dedicated or private where control plane and data plane can be customer-managed.
[01:50] Raj Patel: what's the friction to get started? we prefer self-serve, low-touch, but might need an se-led benchmark.
[01:58] Liam O'Connor: friction is low — sign up, claim free credits, get api key, run quickstart. we'll send a boilerplate chat prompt and sdk snippet. if you want a benchmark, we can run a 1k request perf test on your prompt set to validate latency and cost estimates.
[02:20] Marta Gomez: free credits — how much, and any limits on concurrency?
[02:24] Maya Chen: typical trial credits vary by promo but for plg quickstart we usually provide enough to run a small poc (we'll include amounts in the invite). concurrency is enforced by rate limits per account; we can increase for poc or move to dedicated pools for predictable throughput.
[02:40] Oliver Reed: we also need SOC2 and kyc documents for security review — do you have those?
[02:46] Harper Nguyen: yes, i'll share SOC2 report, data processing agreement, and details on encryption options (KMS, HSM integrations) after this call.
[02:58] Raj Patel: good. also SSO for our console? we use azure ad, sso is must-have for onboarding.
[03:05] Maya Chen: SSO/SAML is supported; we can provision an enterprise org for you, set RBAC roles, and map groups.
[03:14] Marta Gomez: technical: what about kv cache or session state for chat to speed up repeated convo context?
[03:20] Liam O'Connor: we have built-in prefix and kv cache support in the runtime and sdk examples for session management, but for more advanced caching you'd need to colocate with dedicated or private deployments for lowest latencies.
[03:35] Raj Patel: cost is also a concern — we want to balance latency vs unit cost. do you help with suggestions?
[03:41] Maya Chen: yes, our optimize tool recommends batching, quantization, and model variants to reduce per-token costs. for a chat poc, we usually recommend starting with a smaller open model for prototyping, then moving to a higher-quality variant or dedicated capacity for production.
[03:58] Oliver Reed: for dedicated, what's commit minimums look like?
[04:02] Maya Chen: commit sizes vary by region and instance type; i'll send a pricing and dedicated commit sheet but for many mid-market customers we do monthly reserved capacity with burst options.
[04:15] Marta Gomez: any gotchas with the quickstart? like ip allowlists, local firewall rules?
[04:20] Liam O'Connor: just the usual — ensure outbound to our api endpoints, and if you're testing from private infra use a NAT or proxy. for private deployments there's more setup (vpc peering, private control plane) but we have a guided package.
[04:38] Raj Patel: ok next, we need a small checklist for the poc — how fast can we get to first token?
[04:44] Liam O'Connor: if you're self-serve, sign up and run quickstart, typically under an hour for a dev to get first token. we'll send a code snippet; for production-like tests schedule the perf run and we can set up dedicated trial machines.
[05:00] Maya Chen: to recap, we'll share: trial invite + credits, sdk snippets, security pack (soc2, dpa, kms), and a proposed perf test.
[05:08] Raj Patel: sounds good. can you also share any bench comparsion to openai or anthropic on latency/cost?
[05:15] Liam O'Connor: we have public benchmarks for common models, i'll share those links; note benchmarks are workload-dependent.
[05:24] Marta Gomez: one more: do you support streaming response tokens in the python sdk?
[05:28] Liam O'Connor: yes streaming is supported in both node and python sdks, sample code will be in the quickstart repo.
[05:36] Oliver Reed: for compliance, does your hosted retention keep prompt/response logs by default? can we opt-out?
[05:44] Harper Nguyen: hosted has configurable retention and audit logs; we can set shorter retention for dev trials and longer for production as needed. private deployment gives you full control.
[05:58] Raj Patel: timeline — we want POC ready in two weeks, and then decide if we need dedicated by end of quarter.
[06:05] Maya Chen: that's achievable — we'll aim to get you on trial and a perf run scheduled in the next week.
[06:12] Marta Gomez: ok ty, after we get the quickstart we'll try an initial chat flow and surface any blockers.
[06:18] Liam O'Connor: i'll include a sample prompt set and a small benchmark harness you can run locally; if results look off we'll schedule a deeper perf session.
[06:28] Maya Chen: any objections or red flags we should know about?
[06:31] Raj Patel: none yet, just need to validate eu residency and proper slos.
[06:36] Oliver Reed: also want to confirm enterprise sso provisioning time.
[06:40] Harper Nguyen: typically sso setup takes 2-3 business days once we have the account and the metadata.
[06:48] Maya Chen: great, we'll follow up with the items noted. thanks everyone.

End of call.

References/links mentioned: quickstart repo link (sent after), public benchmarks doc, SOC2 report (shared by csm).

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings, speaker overlap, and short pauses removed for readability.
